function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I don’t have access to live market feeds, so I can’t give you the exact spot price of gold for today.  The most reliable way to get the current U.S. gold price is to check one of the following real‑time sources:

| Source | Typical URL | Notes |
|--------|-------------|-------|
| **Bloomberg** | https://www.bloomberg.com/markets/commodities | Provides the U.S. spot price in USD per ounce, updated every few seconds. |
| **Kitco** | https://www.kitco.com/ | Offers a live ticker and charts for gold (and other metals). |
| **Reuters** | https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities | Shows the U.S. spot price and recent price movements. |
| **Investing.com** | https://www.investing.com/commodities/gold | Includes a live chart and the latest price. |
| **NYMEX (CME Group)** | https://www.cmegroup.com/trading/metal/precious.html | For futures prices, but the spot price is usually quoted alongside. |

If you need the price for a specific time (e.g., the closing price on a particular day), most of these sites keep a historical archive that you can search by date.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like help interpreting the data once you have it!
